recipes.name: Shrimp Francesca
ingredients_raw: 1 pound uncooked large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 (8 ounce) can (8 to 10 count) artichoke hearts in water, drained
1 tablespoon finely shredded imported Romano cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Arrange shrimp in the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Gently squeeze any excess liquid from artichoke hearts, break hearts into quarters, and arrange in the spaces between shrimp. Cover with bread crumbs and parsley; sprinkle lemon juice over bread crumbs.
Melt butter with garlic in a small saucepan over medium-low heat; pour butter mixture over bread crumbs. Sprinkle with Romano cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until crumbs and cheese are lightly browned and shrimp turn opaque and orange-pink in color, 10 to 12 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Francesca
raw_recipe.description: This shrimp and artichoke dish is topped with buttery, garlicky bread crumbs and shredded Romano cheese, then baked in the oven until hot and bubbly.

review.reviewBody:
I never liked artichokes before eating this dish but it is outstanding! It tastes like it is from a very fancy restaurant. The one and only creator of this dish, Francesca herself, has made it for me 3 times. She is from Lockport, IL. She created this dish and won 1st place in a local competition with this recipe. She is glad that people are enjoying her recipe.

***
Hi this is Francesca. I am glad you liked the recipe. Here are some hints: I usually serve it with angel hair pasta and steamed brocolli coated in olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper. To make it less fattening, you could substitute olive oil for half of the amount of butter in the Shrimp recipe. It does not change the flavor. You could also add, some cherry tomato cut in half to add more color. You could serve it with some tabasco sauce. Also serve with a glass of medium bodied wine to enhance the flavor of the dish. I would just like to add, that I have always wanted this to become a dish that is served at weddings, for engagement parties as well as the birth of children. In any event, it is a celebratory dish. God Bless All, and thank you for posting my recipe.

I took the advice of another reviewer and added some veggies to make this great recipe a complete, balanced meal. I lined the bottom of the pan with 8 oz raw spinach. I coated the raw shrimp in Old Bay before putting it on top of the spinach. In addition to the artichokes I added broccoli and cauliflower florets (lightly coated in olive oil, minced garlic and Tony Cacheres). 3T butter was plenty for that "scampi" result. Definitely broil at the end to brown the bread crumbs slightly. Yum!

My family loved this recipe. Super easy and quick. I added fresh spinach that I needed to use up. I layered the artichokes and spinach on the bottom of my 9X13 dish then shrimp and remaining ingredients. To wilt the spinach, I added a little chicken broth and baked covered for 10 minutes then removed foil and broiled for a couple more minutes to toast the bread crumbs. Will definitely make this again.

This was so easy and delicious! I chopped up the canned artichokes and patted in between and on top of the shrimp layer. Also small changes- I used about 4 T of fresh chopped parsley, an extra hit on the breadcrumbs and 6 cloves of minced garlic into the butter topping while it was melting. I also increased heat to 425 for the last 10 min of baking for a nice brown on the crumb butter mixture. Made a rice pilaf and a quick salad while it was in the oven- fantastic dinner in 40 minutes-this is a win!

I changed it up a bit - sautéd sliced onions, minced garlic and green peppers in butter, added the shrimp seasoned with seafood seasoning, salt & pepper and then the artichokes with some of the juice then added to the casserole pan, topped with the garlic lemon bread crumbs (garlic in butter, add the bread crumbs until golden and then squeeze half a lemon and continue toasting the bread crumbs) and cheese. Would definitely not drain the artichokes next time. Yummy 
Tried including a picture but it won’t upload

Low Carb version: Ground/fine spicy pork rinds instead of bread crums. Serve over zucchini noodles. Extra garlic and parm is good.
(I added some bacon crums to the dish, is that cheating?)

Fantastic and so easy. Add extra shrimp, some capers and a very generous amount of crumbs and good Pecorino Romano cheese. This can be assembled ahead of time for easy entertainment. Great as a main dish or special appetizer. I often pair this with a nice filet mignon for "surf n turf".

This dish is easy, fast, and tastes like 5 stars! The first time I made it I followed the recipe to the tee. This time, much to my chagrin, I did not have artichokes, so I scrounged for what I had...broccoli, celery, portabello mushrooms, and sweet peppers. I sauteed those veggies in olive oil with garlic, then spread them over the shrimp- which I had seasoned a bit with Hidden Cover Lemon Garlic Blend. I then put the Italian seasoned bread crumb mixture-- which I had to improvise a bit also with shredded sharp cheddar and Romano cheese. This dish is so tasty!
I added halved cherry tomatoes, shaved parmesan instead of Romano , and broiled it for the last min or two. Followed the rest exactly. It was amazing!!!

I loved this recipe, although I did make a few tweaks out of necessity. I couldn't find an 8 oz can of artichokes so I had to use a 14 oz can. Also, I improvised with the bread crumbs and used panko with Italian seasoning added. Everything else stayed the same and I served it on a bed of creamy parmesan risotto. Big hit!
I used artichokes in a jar - I used some of the liquid from the jar ~ I added 1/4 C white wine ~I served it over yellow rice Oh la la

This was delicious! I added a bit more garlic and parsley and made my own Italian bread crumbs with panko and seasoning. The artichokes were incredible with the shrimp. I also added a few scallops which cooked perfectly with the shrimp. I will definitely make this again!

I did add halved cherry tomatoes, on the recommendation of the recipe creator. Would of given 5 stars if the bread crumbs had become more crispy. Still delicious and will make again, per husband's request

This was pretty good, although I did find there was too many breadcrumbs. I used about half the amount and that was plenty. Even then, I found the breadcrumbs got mushy soaked in the butter. The shrimp smelled delicious when cooking. I ended up serving this as an appetizer.
This is a great recipe. My husband said it tastes like something you order at a restaurant. It is so easy to make too
So quick and easy to make. I didn’t change a thing. Delicious!! A keeper for sure!!

Made this for the first time tonight. It was delicious and a big hit. I made a double and kept the recipe as is. Nice combination of buttery garlic and then the tartness of the artichoke. Great recipe and easy. One hint, buy the cut artichoke hearts so you don’t have to quarter when you add them.
